Brand kit · v1.0Designed by
01 · The brief

Inframart has spent seventeen years making other people's products work on real office floors. Acoustics, furniture, water. Five specialist brands, one accountable team. The identity had to do something difficult: stand on its own beside names the client already knows, and look like the company that carries the responsibility.

2009Founded in Bengaluru, by facility managers
5Specialist brands, specified and installed
1Accountable team, one point of contact
27+Named clients, from Microsoft to Asian Paints
02 · The idea

The pillar.

The I of Inframart is drawn as a fluted column, the oldest sign of infrastructure there is. Look closer and it is made of six lines. Five are the brands Inframart brings onto a floor. The sixth is the team that answers for all of them.

  • 01Acoustic360Ceiling rafts, wall panels
  • 02HaworthWorkstations, task seating
  • 03Zip WaterBoiling, chilled, sparkling
  • 04WaterlogicPoint-of-use purification
  • 05ParamountSpecialist range
  • 06One accountable teamSpecify, supply, install, support

Hover a line, or a name. The lines are also what you see in the products: acoustic slats, the fall of water from a tap, the legs of a workstation.

The column stands alone as the monogram.

In the full logo, it opens.

And the name passes through the structure, not on top of it.

Inframart is not a label on a building. It is part of what holds it up.

03 · Construction

Measured, not decorated.

Every part of the mark is set from one unit: X, the cap height of the wordmark. Nothing is placed by eye.

Master artwork: X = 152 px
1XCap height. The unit for everything.
3.59XHeight of the column, top to base.
6 lines~7 px stroke, ~10 px gap, 17 px pitch.
1XMinimum clear space, on all four sides.
04 · The logo

Five versions. One is the default.

05 · Clear space and minimum size

Give it room. Never squeeze it.

The six lines are fine by design, so they are the first thing to break when the logo gets small. We tested it pixel by pixel. Drag to see exactly where it fails.

Clear space · 1X on all sides

Minimum size · live test

60400
300 px · 6/6 lines resolvedPASS

Minimum digital: 200 px wide (300 px preferred). Minimum print: 30 mm wide, to be confirmed on a print proof. Below that, use the monogram.

06 · The monogram

When there is only room for one letter.

The column works alone wherever the full logo would be too small: app icons, favicons, social avatars, a blind emboss on a folder, a foil stamp on a gift box.

10 · The slat

The column, unfolded into a system.

Take the six lines out of the monogram and repeat them, and you get the brand's texture. It is already on the back of the business card. It reads as acoustic slats, as falling water, as a run of desks. It can carry the whole look without another graphic.

Rhythm

Ground
Strength

Behind text, keep it at 25%. Full strength only where nothing sits on top.

Always verticalLines stand up, like the column. Never horizontal, never diagonal.
Same pitchStroke to gap stays 7 : 10, at any size.
Champagne or tintChampagne on teal, or a 25% champagne tint on off-white.
One field per pageOne panel of slats per spread, ideally at an edge.
11 · The brand house

Inframart leads. The partners follow in line.

Clients recognise Haworth and Zip. They should remember Inframart. Whenever partner brands appear with ours, they sit beneath it, in one colour, separated by a champagne point, exactly as on the card.

One colourPartner marks go white on teal, or charcoal on off-white. Their own colours only on their own product sheets.
Never biggerNo partner mark is taller than the Inframart cap height.
Same order, alwaysZip Water · Waterlogic · Haworth · Acoustic360 · Paramount.
12 · Voice

We sound like the people who run the building.

Inframart was started by facility managers. We write the way they talk: plainly, with numbers, and without promising what we can't install. Tap a card to see what we never say.
